To: Supply Chain Leadership Team
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Date: Today
Subject: Balancing delivered cost and carbon in warehouse-to-store shipping under real-world operating rules

Context
Our network ships finished goods from multiple warehouses to multiple retail stores. Each possible warehouse-to-store route carries two important signals: a per‑unit shipping cost and a per‑unit carbon emission rate. In practice these signals conflict—routes that are cheapest to run often have higher emissions—so we must make choices that protect margins while advancing our sustainability commitments. The intent is to meet every store’s demand on time without exceeding available inventory at warehouses, while keeping both spend and emissions within expectations.

Operational rules we must respect
- Route setup/activation costs: Turning on any new warehouse-to-store lane triggers a one-time setup fee covering contract onboarding, compliance paperwork, and dock preparation. A lane is either active or not; if active, the setup fee is incurred regardless of the volume shipped on that lane.
- Minimum order quantities per active lane: Once a lane is activated, we must move at least a specified number of units on it to justify the logistics overhead. Partial truckloads or token shipments are not accepted.
- Limits on suppliers per store: To manage receiving capacity and vendor complexity at our stores, each location may be served by no more than a set number of warehouses. This encourages consolidation and predictable inbound flow.

Management priorities and how we will evaluate options
Leadership has established relative importance weights for delivered cost and emissions. We will score any candidate shipping plan by:
- Multiplying total variable shipping spend by the cost weight.
- Multiplying total emissions by the emissions weight.
- Adding the full (unweighted) setup costs for any lanes we choose to activate.
The preferred plan is the one with the lowest blended total under this scoring. This approach allows us to transparently trade off cost and carbon while fully accounting for the real cash impact of opening lanes.

What the plan must achieve
- Respect warehouse limits: Shipments out of each warehouse must not exceed available inventory.
- Meet store requirements: Each store’s minimum demand must be satisfied within the period.
- Activate lanes judiciously: We only ship on lanes we activate, we pay each activated lane’s setup fee once, and we ship at least the minimum order on those lanes.
- Keep supplier lists tight: Each store draws from no more than the allowed number of warehouses.

Decision and next steps
Our task is to determine which lanes to activate and how much to ship on each active lane to meet demand reliably at the lowest blended total. The output will include:
- The list of active lanes with expected volumes.
- The supplier roster for each store, honoring the maximum supplier limit.
- The resulting totals for variable spend, setup fees, and emissions, along with the blended score under the current weights.
We will also prepare a short sensitivity readout showing how the recommended lane set changes if leadership adjusts the cost or emissions weight. This will equip us to make an informed decision that balances near‑term P&L with our emissions targets.
